ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mary McLeod Bethune

code.originalText: Six-week asthma review: control, inhaler technique and adherence, the ear, nose and throat result, blood pressure and reflux

text.paragraph: Mrs. Bethune returns six weeks after starting budesonide-formoterol. Her nights are better, waking once a week, but she is still breathless on stairs some days and has used the inhaler as a reliever three or four times a week. The dose counter shows she has taken about 70 percent of her maintenance doses: she sometimes forgets the evening dose when she is working late. She saw the ear, nose and throat specialist two weeks ago; nasal endoscopy showed chronic rhinosinusitis without polyps, and her nose is clearer on the steroid spray. Heartburn has gone on omeprazole. Home blood pressure averages 132/78. She has had no ankle swelling on amlodipine and no muscle aches on atorvastatin. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-05-04; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 87.0 kg; blood pressure 134/80, pulse 76; oxygen saturation 97 percent
A few expiratory wheezes on forced expiration

Wheeze, cough and breathlessness for four months: waking with cough and tight chest two or three nights a week, breathless on one flight of stairs, relieved by albuterol, worse with colds, dust and strong scents; known asthma for many years but never confirmed by lung function testing and never treated with an inhaled steroid. Asthma, COPD and heart failure to be distinguished: spirometry with bronchodilator response, FeNO and an echocardiogram booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented chronic asthma. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Blocked nose, thick postnasal drip and a reduced sense of smell for years, worse in the last year; no nosebleeds; never seen by an ear, nose and throat specialist
S — Synthetic upper-airway symptoms; superseded by the diagnosis of chronic rhinosinusitis after nasal endoscopy.
Gastro-esophageal reflux: heartburn and an acid taste two or three evenings a week, worse after late meals and lying down; no trouble swallowing, vomiting, black stools or weight loss
S — Synthetic comorbidity of asthma; not a claim about her real health.
Obesity, class 1 (BMI 33.1); she wants to walk more and to keep up with her work, and agreed to talk about it
S — Synthetic comorbidity recorded in her words and with her agreement; not a claim about her real weight.

Asthma, confirmed: variable airflow obstruction (FEV1 64 percent predicted, rising 270 mL or 21 percent after bronchodilator, with a normal post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.72 and normal DLCO); type 2 inflammation (FeNO 46 ppb, blood eosinophils 0.42 x10^3/uL, total IgE 210, house dust mite sensitization); not COPD and not heart failure. Uncontrolled at diagnosis on albuterol alone
S — Synthetic modern confirmation linked to her documented chronic asthma.

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: clinic blood pressure 152/88 and 146/86, home average 144/84; mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with grade 1 diastolic dysfunction and a normal ejection fraction (62 percent); BNP 48 pg/mL
S — Synthetic finding of the modern work-up; not a claim about her real heart.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 144 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent with hypertension
Chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps: years of congestion, postnasal drip and reduced smell, with mucosal swelling and mucus in both middle meatuses and no polyps on nasal endoscopy
S — Synthetic upper-airway comorbidity of asthma; not a claim about her real health.

list.item:
Asthma on low-dose ICS-formoterol maintenance and reliever (J45.40). Better but not yet well controlled (Asthma Control Test 18). Her technique has three errors and she misses about a third of the maintenance doses, so the treatment has not had a fair trial: GINA advises correcting technique and adherence before stepping up, and that is what we did. [S]
Retrained with a spacer and checked by teach-back.
Evening dose linked to her nightly reading, with a phone reminder.
Same dose; review after any change, or at the next planned visit.
Peak flow diary for two weeks to set her personal best.

Chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps (J32.9). Confirmed on nasal endoscopy; improving on the steroid spray. [S]
Continue fluticasone and saline.

Chronic nasal symptoms (R09.81). Explained by chronic rhinosinusitis; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure (I11.9). Clinic 134/80, home 132/78 on amlodipine; potassium 4.2 and eGFR 64, stable. Near but not yet at target. [S]
Continue amlodipine 5 mg; recheck home readings in a month and add a low-dose thiazide-like diuretic if still above 130/80.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL 88 mg/dL, down 39 percent on atorvastatin; no muscle symptoms. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 20 mg.

Gastro-esophageal reflux (K21.9). Heartburn gone. [S]
Finish the eight weeks of omeprazole in two weeks, then stop and use the meal-timing measures.
